sentences.text:
This appeal u/S 2(1) of Madhya Pradesh Uchha Nyayalay (Khand Nyaypith Ko Appeal) Adhiniyam,
2005 has been filed against the order dated 17.01.2023 and 21.03.2024 passed in W.P. No.
24312/2022 and R.P. No. 199/2023.
2.

sentences.text:
Facts in brief are that in the year 1984, State Government gave land bearing Survey No(s) 250,
263, 264 situated at Village Rajlibey Teh & Distt. Rajgarh on 'patta' to farmers.
One of the Survey No. 250/1/2 admeasuring 2 hectare unirrigated land was given to one Motilal - father of appellant no.1 on patta.
From 1984 till acquisition of land, father of the appellant no.1 was cultivating on the land.

State Government has initiated 2 WA-1648-2024 land acquisition proceedings for total 1,246.37 hectare of land of 09 villages including the village Rajlibey wherein initially 3.772 hectare was acquired and later on 90.410 hectare of land was acquired.

In the second round Survey No.
250/1/2 was acquired.
The land bearing Survey No. 250 was government land and vide order dated 07.04.1984, land bearing survey no. 250/1/2 was given on 'patta' to Motilal and till the year 2009,
name of Motilal
was mentioned in the government record as land owner.

In 2010, three years prior to acquisition of land for dam project, respondent no. 5,6 and their father late Jamnalal purchased land bearing survey no. 250/1/2, 250/1/02,250/1/5,264/1/1,263/1/2,264/1/4 and 264/1/2 admeasuring 14 hectare from the illiterate farmers without mandatory permission from the Collector u/S 165(7-b) of M.P. Land Revenue Code, 1959(referred to as MPLRC hereinafter).

In the year 2013 & 2015, land acquisition proceedings were initiated for construction of Mohanpura Dam Kailash Dangi vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 7 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/127054756/
1 Project.

sentences.text: Respondent no. 5,6 and their father Jamnalal received the whole amount of compensation given by the respondent no.1 to 4 for all survey numbers.

Compensation was paid without verifying the fact that land Survey No. 250/1/2 is government land whose patta was given to Motilal in 1984 and, therefore no right of respondent no.5 was created on the said survey number.

Even otherwise,
the land bearing survey no. 250/1/2 neither came under submerged area nor in catchment area of dam.
Respondent no.7,8 and 9 are having illegal possession of land and cultivating on the same.
Despite passage of 5 years of acquisition, the land remained unutilized for the purpose for which it was acquired .
Various complaints and representations have been filed before the 3 WA-1648-2024 respondents no.1 to 4, but no action has been taken.

Thereafter, the appellants had approached this Court in writ petition for return of land and its possession as well as for conducting inquiry as there was loss of government money which was given as compensation to those who have no entitlement for the same.
However, learned Single Judge has dismissed the writ petition.
Being aggrieved, the appellants have filed this Court appeal.
3. Learned counsel for the appellants submitted that learned Single Judge erred in dismissing the writ petition only on the ground of limitation.

Although, as per Section 101 of Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013,
return of land can be initiated only after completion of 5 years and, therefore, the cause of action for return of land commences on 17.11.2020.

entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: Time period for legal action from 15.03.2020 till 28.02.2022 is excluded in view of outbreak of Covid-19 Pandemic.
Writ petition was filed on 27.10.2022 after obtaining certified copies of the awards and revenue records.
The father of appellant no.1 filed appeal before the SDM, Rajgarh against mutation on 04.02.16 which was rejected.
Thereafter, appeal was filed before the Commissioner during his life.
After his death, the appeal was withdrawn on 15.11.2017.
Appellants came to know about dismissal of appeal in January 2020.
Appellants filed complaint before the Chief Minister through CM Helpline, but did not get any relief.
Thereafter, appellants obtained certified copies of award and map on 16.06.2022 and 11.07.2022.
The representations and complaints filed by the appellants are still pending.
Hence cause of action still survives.
Accordingly, writ petition was filed.
4 WA-1648-2024 Learned Single Judge without considering the chequered history has passed the order on the ground of limitation.
4. Learned Single Judge further erred by drawing conclusion that no objections were raised when the award was passed.

However, it is pertinent to mention that late Motilal and other affected families preferred representations before the Sub Divisional Officer on 10.02.2016 for restricting disbursement of amount of compensation to respondents no. 5 ,6 and their father, but they were put to deaf ears.

The Sub Divisional Officer was the Land Acquisition Officer dealing with the entire matter of appeal against mutation and objection/representations filed by the aggrieved parties in land acquisition proceedings.
He was well aware of all the facts.
Despite that, compensation was paid.
Name of Mahesh was mutated in the revenue records on 16.10.2010, against which an appeal was filed by Motilal - father of appellants which was dismissed on the ground of delay by the SDO.
Learned Single Judge dismissed the petition by holding that the appellants are having remedy to challenge the sale deeds.

It is pertinent to mention that land was given by the State Government to Kailash Dangi vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 7 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/127054756/

sentences.text: Late Motilal on 'patta' and sale deed dated 08.06.2010 was executed without taking permission from the Collector in utter violation of Section 165(6), 165(7-b) of MPLRC and therefore, the same is illegal and void-ab-initio.

5 . On the other hand, learned counsel for the respondent/State submitted that learned Single has dismissed the petition on the ground of delay in as much as that challenge was made to the award passed in the year 2014-15 in the year 2022.
No objections were raised at the time of passing of 5 WA-1648-2024 award.
Despite availability of alternative remedy, appellants have approached this Court and therefore, petition was dismissed as not maintainable.
Under such circumstances, no interference is warranted in the order passed by learned Single Judge.
6. We have heard, learned counsel for the parties and perused the record.
7. Admittedly, the award was passed way back in 2014-15 and challenge to the said award was made in the year 2022.

The reasons assigned for delay in filing the petition cannot be accepted as no cause of action arises for consideration in the year 2022 for the award passed in the year 2014-15 wherein compensation had also been disbursed.

8. Learned Single Judge has rightly held that when Jamnalal alias Jamnaprasad purchased the land which originally belongs to government and was given on 'patta' to Late Motilal in the year 1984 by registered sale deeds and after the death of Jamnalal, when it got mutated in the name of his son Mahesh in the year 2010, Motilal has challenged the mutation proceedings before the SDO, but the same were dismissed having been filed belatedly.

It has further been held that revenue authorities are not competent to go into veracity of sale deed or to declare the same as null and void and that Motilal should have challenged the sale deeds and not the mutation proceedings.
Even after his death, his legal heirs i.e. the appellants herein should have challenged the sale deeds which has not been done.

9. In view of the aforesaid, learned Single Judge has not committed any error warranting interference in the order impugned.
6 WA-1648-2024 10.
Consequently, appeal fails and is hereby dismissed.
However, liberty is granted to the appellants to avail appropriate remedy available under the law.
